steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Concept: Waves are the primary agent of coastal change. They are generated by wind blowing over the sea surface. The size and energy of waves depend on wind speed, wind duration, and fetch (the distance of open water over which the wind blows). | Definition: Weathering is the breakdown of rock in situ (in its original place) by physical, chemical or biological processes. It does not involve transport - that is erosion. | Definition: Mass movement is the downhill movement of material under gravity. It is especially important at the coast where cliffs are unstable. Water plays a key role in making material heavier and reducing friction. | Definition: Coastal erosion is the wearing away of the coastline by the sea.
